    Local endomorphism rings of finite-dimensional indecomposable modules #

    Fitting decomposition shows that every endomorphism of a finite-dimensional indecomposable module is either invertible or nilpotent. Consequently its endomorphism ring is local.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.nonempty_iso_of_isUnit_comp {C : Type u_1} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] {X Y : C} [Nontrivial (CategoryTheory.End X)] [IsLocalRing (CategoryTheory.End Y)] (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ X) (hfg : IsUnit (CategoryTheory.End.of (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f g))) :
    Nonempty (X ≅ Y)

    If End(X) is nontrivial and End(Y) is local, then a pair of maps X ⟶ Y ⟶ X with invertible composite exhibits X and Y as isomorphic. This is the categorical form of the fact that a nonzero retract of an object with local endomorphism ring is the whole object.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.isUnit_or_isNilpotent_of_finite_indecomposable {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [Module.Finite k A] (M : ModuleCat A) [Module.Finite k ↑M] (hM : CategoryTheory.Indecomposable M) (f : CategoryTheory.End M) :
    IsUnit f ∨ IsNilpotent f

    A finite-dimensional indecomposable module has the Fitting alternative: each endomorphism is invertible or nilpotent.

    IsLocalRing (CategoryTheory.End M)

    The categorical endomorphism ring of a finite-dimensional indecomposable module is local.
